source.title: Study on the Large Batch Size Training of Neural Networks Based on the Second Order Gradient

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; figures are represented without readable numerical values.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies batch size and reports AlexNet accuracy on CIFAR-10, addressing the large-batch generalization gap with its own experiment.
record.gate_note: Figure 1 is the paper's reimplementation of the batch-size/accuracy comparison. Other experiments report accuracy or training performance, but do not clearly identify a held-out test measure in the supplied text. Cited prior work is not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study investigates large-batch optimization, but its own results do not establish held-out performance under a fixed epoch budget. Figure 1's accuracy split and training budget are unspecified; later accuracy comparisons concern training performance. These results cannot establish V5's generalization penalty or its removal.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' claims: they attribute large-batch difficulties to diminishing gradients and parameter updates, predict worsening generalization with larger batches, and claim improvements from sample filtering and batch scheduling. However, the supplied results do not establish held-out generalization improvements. The authors also report that their median-curvature optimizer approximates LARS performance at smaller batches and deteriorates at larger batches.
record.recipe_differences: AlexNet on CIFAR-10 is used to reimplement the large-batch accuracy problem; the supplied text does not specify Figure 1's epoch budget or whether accuracy is held out.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size; the paper reports different loss-curve fluctuation amplitudes for small, medium, and large batches.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger batches reduce measured gradients and parameter-update strides; the authors interpret these as explanations of training difficulty.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch size affects optimization dynamics in AlexNet on CIFAR-10.

fits_no_version.finding: Discarding small-loss samples improves reported training accuracy at batches 2000 and 8000; reducing first-epoch batch size together with learning rate improves reported training performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sample filtering and an initial batch-size/learning-rate change can improve large-batch optimization.

record.problems: Figure 1 values are figure-only in the supplied text, and the text does not specify whether its accuracy measure is held out or its epoch budget. Some reported standard-deviation bars are mentioned for other experiments, but not for Figure 1.
record.rows_left_out: Figures 10–14 compare training accuracy or training performance after discarding small-loss samples or reducing the first-epoch batch size; the text does not establish these as held-out results. Figure 16 compares training accuracy for median-curvature and LARS. These do not provide extractable held-out results for the listed claim versions.

record.verdict_notes: The authors' generalization terminology does not resolve the unspecified accuracy split or epoch budget. Their curvature analysis does not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization correlation. Results already declared in rows_left_out are not repeated as missing.

rows.subject: AlexNet
rows.operation_detail: Compared accuracy across batch sizes on CIFAR-10.
rows.note: The text calls this a reimplementation of the large-batch problem, but gives no numerical values or explicit statement identifying the accuracy as held-out accuracy.
rows.check: Figure 1 does not identify accuracy as held-out or specify a fixed epoch budget, and its plotted values are unreadable in the supplied text. The 32–60000 batch-size range is explicitly given for Figure 3's first-step gradient experiment, not Figure 1.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
